Root at 50/2.5/2.5/0.35 converged but cost $190M/yr and sent about 342 mol/s C5 to B. T is being split into C5 bottoms and C4-and-lighter tops; TT makes C4 bottoms; TTT removes ethane so C3 blend can sell. These blends are worth roughly $618M, $186M and $73M/yr at full recovery. note: I’m strengthening all three light-end splits and operating closer to feed pressure; this should qualify the valuable C4 and C5 blends while reducing refrigeration expense.
notebook: PLAN: Build a blend-oriented flowsheet: root C5/C6 split; lights make C3, C4 and C5 cuts; heavies isolate C6 and recover heavy products. Step 3: increase light-section separation and raise operating pressure to cut refrigeration cost; then add heavy branches only where margins justify cost. Prior root 50/2.5/2.5/.35 cost $190M and leaked C5 both ways. T split was too weak: TT retained 120 mol/s butane and TTB retained 95 propane, so neither C4 nor C5 blend qualified. TTT successfully made saleable C3 worth $35M. Full-recovery blend values are about C3 $73M, C4 $186M, C5 $719M. Testing 60/4 root, 50/4 de-C5, 45/4 C3/C4 at low pressure drop.

A successful root side draw could eliminate the $70M de-pentanizer and greatly improve recovery.

note: I’m replacing the unsuccessful side-draw scheme with a conventional four-column blend train. Clean sequential cuts should recover the C3, C4, and C5 blends and generate enough revenue to exceed column costs.

note: The low-energy design has no saleable products. I’m raising separation power on all three easy blend cuts to establish positive revenue before optimizing costs.
notebook: PLAN: Three-column blend train: root C4/C5 split, C3/C4 splitter on tops, C5/C6 splitter on bottoms. First establish all three blends at effective reflux, then reduce cost. note: The equal reflux and boil-up settings forced far too much material overhead. I’m matching boil-up to each target cut while retaining enough reflux for blend purity.
notebook: PLAN: Three-column blend train: root C4/C5 split, C3/C4 splitter on tops, C5/C6 splitter on bottoms. Set boil-up from the desired distillate fraction, establish qualifying blends, then reduce cost. Key diagnosis: previous R=B=4 forced ~44% distillate, whereas root needs 26%; excess boil-up pulled C5 overhead and C4 into C5 product. Use root R6/B2.5, C3 splitter R5/B3.5, C5 splitter R5/B2.2. Revenues if qualified: C3 ~$73M, C4 ~$186M, C5 ~$618M.
